approach: Integrate the velocity function with respect to time, using the given position at t = 0 to fix the constant, then evaluate at t = 2 s.

steps.text: Integrate v(t) to get x(t), since velocity is the derivative of position.
steps.equation: x(t) = ∫(1 − 3t² + 2t³) dt = t − t³ + t⁴/2 + C

steps.text: Use the condition x(0) = 0 to find the constant of integration.

common_mistakes.text: Leaving the constant term of the velocity unintegrated, writing its contribution as 1 instead of t, while integrating the other two terms correctly, which gives 1 m.
Making a power-rule slip while integrating the −3t² term, treating its antiderivative as −3t instead of −t³, which changes the answer to 4 m.
Dropping the minus sign while integrating the −3t² term, so it contributes +t³ instead of −t³, which gives 2 + 8 + 8 = 18 m.
